name: Route Basic Auth
description: Adds HTTP Basic authentication to configured routes (constant-time credential comparison).
project_description:
The Route Basic Authentication module protects configured routes with HTTP basic authentication. The routes are configured with the Drupal route name (described as machine name in the structure of routes documentation), for example the login: user.login . The HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, ...) that should be protected by HTTP basic authentication are also configured for each route.

 A site wide username and password is used by default, configurable on the settings page (Administration » Configuration » System » Route Basic Authentication settings). Individual routes can use their own credentials instead of the site-wide pair.

 Back to top 

 What's new in 2.1 
 The 2.1 line is available as a beta ( 2.1.0-beta1 ) to allow the new configuration surface and upgrade path a period of real-world testing.

 Per-route credentials 
 Each protected route can use its own username and password instead of only the site-wide pair. Without custom credentials, a route falls back to the site-wide credentials as before.

 Key module integration 
 With the Key module installed, the password can come from a password key (an environment variable, a file outside the web root, and so on) instead of a plain text field. When a key is selected the password field is hidden and any stored password value is removed from configuration. This works for both site-wide and per-route credentials.

 Settings UI for protected routes 
 Protected routes are now added, removed, and configured directly on the settings page, shown as a compact table with a checkbox per HTTP method. Editing configuration directly is still possible; the stored format changed in 2.1 and existing configuration is converted automatically when you run database updates.

 Drupal 12 and reworked internals 
 2.1 adds Drupal 12 compatibility and reworks the authentication internals (credential extraction, validation, resolution, and flood handling are now separate services). As a result, supported core for this version is ^11.3 || ^12 .

 Back to top 

 Installation 
 Install as you would normally install a contributed Drupal module. Visit Installing modules for further information.

 Back to top 

 Configuration 
 Configure user permissions in Administration » People » Permissions:

 
 Change the Route Basic Authentication settings : permission to change the module settings. 
 
 Configure the username and password on the settings page or in the route_basic_auth.settings.yml configuration file. Installing the Key module and selecting a password key is strongly recommended: without it, passwords are stored in plain text in site configuration, which means they end up in the database, in every configuration export, and in every backup.

 Configure the routes that should be protected on the settings page: enter the route name (for example user.login ), check the HTTP methods to protect, and use Add another route for more. Each route can use its own credentials by checking Custom credentials . Prior to 2.1 routes could only be defined in configuration.

 Routes can still be defined in the route_basic_auth.settings.yml configuration file. As of 2.1 the format is a list (the credentials mapping is optional; without it the site-wide credentials are used):

 protected_routes:
 - name: 'user.login'
 methods:
 - 'GET'
 - name: 'user.login.http'
 methods:
 - 'POST'
 credentials:
 username: 'login-http-user'
 password: 'login-http-password'
 password_key: '' Back to top 

 Flood protection 
 Flood protection reuses the IP limit of core's user.flood settings (by default 50 failed attempts per hour per IP). Only requests that actually supply credentials count as failed attempts. Once the limit is reached, further requests from that IP are denied with a 403, valid credentials included, until the window expires. This matches how core handles login flooding.
